name: PaceKeeper
oneLineDescription: A single-user personal running log app for recording and viewing runs with calculated pace.
whatItIs: PaceKeeper is a personal running log application where a single user can record runs by entering a date, distance (in kilometers), and duration (in minutes). The app displays all logged runs in reverse chronological order with automatically calculated pace (min/km), allows deletion of individual runs, and persists data in a local JSON file on the server. There is no authentication, no database, and no multi-user support. The UI is built with Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, and CSS Modules, and is intended to be functional on both mobile and desktop.

stack.name: next
stack.purpose: App Router framework for routing, server actions, and rendering

coreUserFlows: User fills out the add-run form with a date, distance, and duration, submits it, and sees the new run appear in the list.
User views the home page and sees all past runs sorted most-recent-first, each showing date, distance, duration, and calculated pace.
User clicks the delete control on a run and it is immediately removed from the list and from storage.
User visits the app with no runs logged and sees the empty-state message 'No runs yet. Add your first run!'

dataModel.purpose: Stores a single logged run with its date, distance, and duration, persisted in a local JSON file.

crossCuttingPrinciples: The application is single-user only with no user identification or authentication anywhere in the stack.
All data persists in a local JSON file via server-side read/write operations; there is no database.
Distance is always stored and displayed in kilometers; duration is always stored and displayed in minutes — no unit conversion.
Malformed storage data must fail gracefully with a logged error rather than crashing the app.
Styling must use CSS Modules exclusively — no external CSS frameworks are permitted.
The UI must be responsive and functional on both mobile and desktop.
specSummary: PaceKeeper is a minimal, single-user running log built with Next.js 14 (App Router) and TypeScript, styled with CSS Modules, and persisting data in a local JSON file on the server — no database, no authentication. The product has five features implemented in a defined order. First, a foundational storage layer defines the Run data shape (id, date as ISO string, distanceKm, durationMin) and provides server-side read, add, and delete operations against a JSON file, with graceful handling of empty or malformed data. Second, the home page displays all runs sorted most-recent-first, showing formatted date, distance, duration, and pace calculated as durationMin divided by distanceKm to two decimal places, with an empty-state message when no runs exist. Third, an inline form above the run list lets the user log a new run with a date picker, distance input, and duration input; all fields are required, distance and duration must be positive, and the date cannot be in the future — validation errors appear inline and the form clears after successful submission. Fourth, each run in the list has a delete control that immediately removes the run from storage and updates the list, with no confirmation dialog. Fifth, basic responsive styling is applied using CSS Modules to cover layout, typography, form inputs with focus and error states, and styled buttons with hover and active states. Dark mode, editing runs, analytics, GPX import, mile conversion, PWA features, and deployment configuration are all explicitly out of scope.
